Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with throughput and the routing policies. Before we finalize the Order Form, our security team has a couple of open asks that will need to be reflected in the MSA or an attached exhibit:

- SOC 2: we need confirmation of the current SOC 2 report period and a statement about how we’ll be notified of future reports (push or pull).
- Pen-test: sample language we typically ask for is a bounded inspection/pen-test window clause (e.g., notice period, staging access only, redaction rules in reports). We need to ensure any vulnerability details shared are redacted for customer privacy.
- Evidence cadence: we prefer an evidence upload cadence (quarterly) and a named evidentiary owner for requests.
- Scope: we only require production logs on an as-requested basis with RBAC — we prefer ephemeral (time-limited) access tokens for live inspections.

I attached a short questionnaire (Medallion_Security_Questions.pdf) and highlighted the areas we view as must-haves. Can you loop in legal and your assurance lead so we can align on precise clause text and an evidence cadence?

Can we aim to close this by end of next week (9/19) so procurement can circulate an internal PO?

Thanks,

High level from product/sales:
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II (report covers 2027-09 through 2028-08). We can provide a certified report and a push notification to a named contact when new reports are available.
- Pen-test: we are comfortable with a bounded inspection approach: staging tenant access, 14-day notice, and an agreed CVE redaction process for any customer-shared reports.

- Access: ephemeral IAM tokens + minimal scoped roles for the inspection period.

Rishi / Monica / Jane — thanks, I reviewed the questionnaire and Rishi’s proposed approach. I drafted a compact exhibit that aims to balance Medallion’s audit needs with Redwood’s operational constraints. High-level summary of the redlines and rationale: 

1) Bounded inspection clause (MSA Exhibit A3):
- Notice: 14 calendar days prior written notice to the Redwood security contact.
- Environment: inspection restricted to a non-production staging tenant unless explicitly agreed for a one-off production review with additional safeguards.
- Duration: max 5 business days of direct access; further review to be supported by exported artifacts (logs, packet captures) rather than continued interactive sessions.

2) Pen-test report handling and redaction:
- Redwood will provide a pen-test summary with vulnerability severities and remediation timelines. Detailed exploit steps and PII/credentials will be redacted before customer delivery.
- For critical findings affecting multiple customers, Redwood will notify affected customers under our incident process — not through the audit exhibit.

3) SOC 2 report delivery and retention:
- Redwood will provide the last SOC 2 Type II report upon execution of the exhibit and will notify the primary security contact within 7 days of issuance of future reports.

4) Evidence cadence and owner:
- Evidence cadence: quarterly uploads to a secure, access-controlled folder. Each upload includes the evidence manifest and contact owner.
- Ownership: Redwood primary evidence owner: Monica Patel (monica_patel@redwoodinference.com). Medallion evidence owner to be named in the Order Form.

5) Access controls (ops bullets):
- Ephemeral tokens, time-boxed roles, and scoped read-only access.
- Audit logs of inspection sessions retained for 90 days and accessible to Medallion on request (summary-level).

Proposed next steps: 
- Jane/legal: confirm whether Medallion needs production access for any use cases and if so, list them now.
- Rishi: if Medallion approves, we’ll insert the exhibit into the MSA redline and circulate a DocuSign packet for signature.
- Monica: can you finalize the evidence-sprint calendar (upload format, manifest fields) and add operational instructions for staging tenant onboarding?

I’ve attached the proposed exhibit text as redline_MSA_proposed_clauses.docx. I kept language short — legal prefers exhibit-level clarity rather than scattering obligations across the MSA and Order Form. If Medallion requires a separate data processing addendum for artifact delivery, we can coordinate that too.

Laura Bennett
